title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
tempo_note: PianoFlow teaching suggestion; LearnPianoGame plays it at 100, Pianomi at 88.
keyboard: Fits the GarageKey Mini range C3–C6 (MIDI 48–84). Melody is C4–G4; left hand stays on or above C3.
setting: PianoFlow teaching setting: verified traditional melody in the right hand, in C major; the left-hand roots and blocked C and G chords are written for this catalog, not taken from a source arrangement.
lyric_snippet: Mary had a little lamb, little lamb, little lamb, Mary had a little lamb, its fleece was white as snow.

sources.title: LearnPianoGame, Mary Had a Little Lamb, letter notes
sources.used_for: Note-level source: melody bar by bar with octaves and beat lengths (E4 D4 C4 D4 | E4 E4 E4(2) | D4 D4 D4(2) | E4 G4 G4(2) | E4 D4 C4 D4 | E4 E4 E4 E4 | D4 D4 E4 D4 | C4(4)), 4/4, C major, range C4–G4. Its chord names (C C G C C C G C) agree with this setting's harmony; its arrangement was not copied.

sources.title: Pianomi, Mary Had a Little Lamb, easy piano letter notes
sources.used_for: Independent note-level cross-check: the same pitches bar by bar in C major, 4/4, 8 bars, with half notes at the ends of bars 2–4. Its left-hand part (which goes down to G2) was not used.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Mary Had a Little Lamb
sources.used_for: Text and history only: Hale's poem first published in 1830 (Poems for Our Children, Marsh, Capen & Lyon); today it is sung to the “Merrily We Roll Along” tune, not Lowell Mason's 1830s setting.

variants: The tune used here is the one commonly sung today (also the tune of “Merrily We Roll Along”). Lowell Mason set Hale's words to a different melody in the 1830s (Juvenile Lyre, 1831); that setting has fallen out of use and was not used. Both note-level sources agree on every pitch and bar line in C major. Some arrangements put the G chord's bass on G2 (Pianomi); this setting keeps the left hand at or above C3 by playing the G chord as D3 G3 B3.

sections.name: Its fleece was white as snow

notes.five-finger-position: Four keys (C, D, E, G) under one C-position hand; quarters and halves only, so One-Hand Melody is not scored separately.
notes.hands-together: LH changes only on beats 1 and 3, always with a RH note.
notes.basic-chords: Slow half-note triads in one close grip.
notes.inversions: The G chord is played with D at the bottom (D3 G3 B3), which keeps the left hand at or above C3.

ladder.label: Right hand alone
ladder.play: RH, thumb on middle C: E D C D | E E E(half) | D D D(half) | E G G(half). Fingers 3-2-1-2 | 3-3-3 | 2-2-2 | 3-5-5. About 100 quarter notes a minute.

ladder.label: Right hand and left-hand roots
ladder.play: RH as before; LH holds one whole note per bar: C3 (bars 1-2), G3 (bar 3), C3 (bar 4).

ladder.label: Both hands (teaching setting)
ladder.play: RH as before; LH plays two half-note chords per bar: C3 E3 G3 (bars 1-2 and 4), D3 G3 B3 (bar 3).

phrases.name: Its fleece was white as snow

notes.five-finger-position: Same four keys; bar 7 turns back up to E before the close on C.
notes.hands-together: Same once-or-twice-a-bar LH changes; the last bar is held by both hands.
notes.basic-chords: Slow half-note triads in one close grip, ending on a held C chord.
notes.inversions: Same D3 G3 B3 shape for the G chord in bar 7.

ladder.label: Right hand alone
ladder.play: RH, thumb on middle C: E D C D | E E E E | D D E D | C(whole). Fingers 3-2-1-2 | 3-3-3-3 | 2-2-3-2 | 1.

ladder.label: Right hand and left-hand roots
ladder.play: RH as before; LH holds C3 (bars 5-6), G3 (bar 7), C3 (bar 8).

ladder.label: Both hands (teaching setting)
ladder.play: RH as before; LH half-note chords C3 E3 G3 (bars 5-6), D3 G3 B3 (bar 7), and a whole-note C3 E3 G3 under the final 'snow.'

score_note: Catalog-relative whole-piece 0–10 score from pianoflow/tools/score_pieces.py after Mary Had a Little Lamb was added. Raw = w1 + 0.35·w2 + 0.2·w3 + min(0.1·sum(rest), 2.0) on tagged technique weights; score = 0.3 + (raw − min_raw)/(max_raw − min_raw)·9.6. Basic chords (peak 0.9) and inversions (peak 0.6) appear in the full-rung instance scores but are below the tag thresholds (0.5 × weight: 1.0 and 1.5), so they are not tagged on the whole piece. Adding a piece can shift other catalog scores slightly (the formula is catalog-relative).
